papers.title: OPTIMIZING CLOUD RESOURCE ALLOCATION USING MULTI AGENT DEEP REINFORCEMENT LEARNING-BASED ADAPTIVE HHO ALGORITHM
papers.abstract: Cloud computing workloads are projected to grow by 23.1% annually, with over 80% of enterprises adopting multi-cloud strategies, creating a pressing need for optimal virtual machine (VM) resource allocation to ensure cost efficiency and performance. However, existing allocation strategies suffer from static optimization limitations and inefficient adaptation to dynamic workloads, leading to frequent resource underutilization and service delays. To address these issues, this work proposes a novel Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (MADRL-AHHO) algorithm for cloud resource allocation using the VM Resource Allocation dataset (VM-0 to VM-5 classes). Initially, the dataset is preprocessed through normalization and feature selection to reduce dimensionality and noise. Feature extraction is enhanced using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) integrated with Firefly Optimization (CNN-FFO), which is benchmarked for learning capacity and solution convergence. However, performance limitations in CNN-FFO under dynamic load conditions are overcome by integrating CNN with Adaptive Harris Hawks Optimization (CNN-AHHO), which dynamically adjusts its exploration and exploitation capabilities based on multi-agent reinforcement feedback. The agents interact with the environment to learn optimal VM allocation policies by maximizing resource utilization and minimizing SLA violations. Experimental results demonstrate that CNN-AHHO outperforms CNN-FFO and traditional machine learning methods in terms of allocation accuracy, convergence rate, and computational efficiency, thereby offering a robust and adaptive solution for cloud infrastructure management.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Scalable Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Joint Resource Optimization in Cloud–Edge–End Video Streaming Systems
papers.abstract: Cloud-edge-end (CEE) collaboration has demonstrated significant potential in video streaming analysis. However, dynamic wireless environments, lack of incentive mechanisms, and constrained resources (e.g., transmission power, bandwidth, and computing resources) remain the primary bottlenecks for achieving efficient CEE-based video processing. To address these challenges, this paper focuses on a multi-user CEE scenario with dynamic wireless channels and investigates the joint optimization of adaptive incentives, cooperative offloading, and resource allocation. We propose a novel framework, called JROC, to motivate edge devices (EDs) to participate in collaborative computation within CEE, thereby enhancing system utility. Specifically, JROC encompasses a smart contract-based adaptive incentive mechanism and an Adaptive Transformer-based multi-agent reinforcement Learning Algorithm (ATLA). The incentive mechanism leverages blockchain to ensure trustworthy and automated incentive distribution, while ATLA captures long-term dependencies and global state features among agents to guide video tasks in dynamic environments through adaptive compression, cooperative offloading, and resource allocation. Moreover, we discuss key steps for deploying the proposed algorithm in a real CEE prototype, including lightweight actor inference at the terminal side and training at the edge. Experimental results based on a real-world operator dataset show that, compared to existing methods, JROC achieves higher long-term system utility while maintaining favorable scalability, thereby validating its effectiveness in resource-constrained and under-incentivized CEE video streaming scenarios.

papers.title: Mobility-Aware Resource Allocation for mmWave IAB Networks: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.abstract: MmWaves have been envisioned as a promising direction to provide Gbps wireless access. However, they are susceptible to high path losses and blockages, which directional antennas can only partially mitigate. That makes mmWave networks coverage-limited, thus requiring dense deployments. Integrated access and backhaul (IAB) architectures have emerged as a cost-effective solution for network densification. Resource allocation in mmWave IAB networks must face big challenges to cope with heavy temporal dynamics, such as intermittent links caused by user mobility and blockages from moving obstacles. This makes it extremely difficult to find optimal and adaptive solutions. In this article, exploiting the distributed structure of the problem, we propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to optimize user throughput via flow routing and link scheduling in mmWave IAB networks characterized by user mobility and link outages generated by moving obstacles. The proposed approach implicitly captures the environment dynamics, coordinates the interference, and manages the buffer levels of IAB relay nodes. We design different MARL components, considering full-duplex and half-duplex IAB-nodes. In addition, we provide a communication and coordination scheme for RL agents in an online training framework, addressing the feasibility issues of practical systems. Numerical results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Efficient Resource Allocation for On-Demand Mobile-Edge Cloud Computing
papers.abstract: Mobile-edge cloud computing is a new paradigm to provide cloud computing capabilities at the edge of pervasive radio access networks in close proximity to mobile users. Aiming at provisioning flexible on-demand mobile-edge cloud service, in this paper we propose a comprehensive framework consisting of a resource-efficient computation offloading mechanism for users and a joint communication and computation (JCC) resource allocation mechanism for network operator. Specifically, we first study the resource-efficient computation offloading problem for a user, in order to reduce user's resource occupation by determining its optimal communication and computation resource profile with minimum resource occupation and meanwhile satisfying the QoS constraint. We then tackle the critical problem of user admission control for JCC resource allocation, in order to properly select the set of users for resource demand satisfaction. We show the admission control problem is NP-hard, and hence develop an efficient approximation solution of a low complexity by carefully designing the user ranking criteria and rigourously derive its performance guarantee. To prevent the manipulation that some users may untruthfully report their valuations in acquiring mobile-edge cloud service, we further resort to the powerful tool of critical value approach to design truthful pricing scheme for JCC resource allocation. Extensive performance evaluation demonstrates that the proposed schemes can achieve superior performance for on-demand mobile-edge cloud computing.

summary: The literature on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing emphasizes the need for adaptive strategies to optimize resource distribution in cloud and edge environments, particularly under varying workloads and user demands. Key studies highlight innovative algorithms like the Adaptive Transformer-based MARL and the MADRL-AHHO algorithm, which improve efficiency but face challenges in scalability and real-world implementation. Gaps identified include the lack of comprehensive solutions integrating incentive mechanisms for collaboration and the need for robust performance under extreme dynamic conditions.
scholarly_positioning: Existing research on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for resource allocation in cloud computing has primarily focused on optimizing strategies for static workloads, often neglecting the complexities introduced by dynamic user demands and environmental conditions. While algorithms like the Adaptive Transformer-based MARL and MADRL-AHHO have shown promise in improving resource efficiency, they fall short in scalability and practical implementation, particularly in real-world scenarios. Furthermore, the lack of integrated incentive mechanisms for collaboration among edge devices presents a significant gap in current methodologies. This proposed research aims to address these unresolved tensions by developing a novel MARL framework that not only adapts to dynamic workloads but also incorporates collaborative incentives, thereby contributing to a more robust and scalable solution for resource allocation in cloud environments.
research_scope: This study will focus on the development of a novel Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework tailored for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing environments, specifically targeting video streaming applications. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the framework's performance will be assessed against traditional static resource allocation methods. A control group will consist of existing MARL algorithms without collaborative incentives. Primary outcomes will include resource allocation efficiency, measured by system utility and throughput, while secondary outcomes will evaluate scalability and adaptability under varying user demands and environmental conditions. The research aims to demonstrate the effectiveness of integrated collaborative incentives in enhancing resource utilization and system performance in real-world cloud scenarios.
concept_definition: 1. Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL): A machine learning approach where multiple agents learn to make decisions through interactions in an environment, optimizing their strategies based on rewards. 2. Dynamic Resource Allocation: The process of distributing computing resources in real-time based on changing demands and workloads, particularly in cloud environments. 3. Collaborative Incentives: Mechanisms designed to encourage agents to work together, sharing information and strategies to improve overall system performance. 4. System Utility: A measure of the overall effectiveness and satisfaction derived from resource allocation, often quantified in terms of performance metrics like throughput. 5. Throughput: The amount of data successfully processed or transmitted in a given time period, indicating the efficiency of resource utilization. 6. Scalability: The ability of the resource allocation framework to maintain performance as the number of users or workload increases. 7. Adaptability: The capacity of the system to adjust resource allocation strategies in response to varying user demands and environmental conditions. 8. Ablation Studies: Experimental analyses that involve systematically removing or altering components of the framework to assess their impact on performance outcomes. 9. Control Group: A baseline comparison group in an experiment that uses existing MARL algorithms without collaborative incentives to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. 10. Quality of Service (QoS): A measure of the overall performance of a service, particularly in terms of latency, reliability, and user satisfaction, crucial for real-time applications like video streaming.
technical_feasibility: The proposed study is technically feasible, requiring access to open-source MARL frameworks for development and experimentation. It will need GPU resources for training and evaluation of the models. No hidden state extraction or labeled datasets are necessary as the focus is on dynamic resource allocation strategies rather than internal representations. The study does not involve human participants, thus ethics approval is not required. To enhance the robustness of the findings, it would be beneficial to include diverse workload scenarios and possibly real-world deployment data for validation. A feasible adjustment could involve simulating user demands and workloads instead of relying on actual data.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) in optimizing resource allocation in cloud computing environments, particularly under static workloads; however, they treat dynamic user demands and collaborative incentives among edge devices as secondary or unresolved, leaving unclear whether these factors significantly enhance resource utilization and system performance. This matters practically because efficient resource allocation is critical for maintaining quality of service in real-time applications like video streaming; therefore, this study investigates the integration of collaborative incentives and adaptive strategies in MARL for dynamic resource allocation within cloud environments.
question: How does the integration of collaborative incentives within a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning framework affect resource allocation efficiency and system performance in dynamic cloud computing environments for video streaming applications compared to traditional static resource allocation methods?
theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research integrates collaborative incentives (independent variable) within a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to enhance resource allocation efficiency (dependent variable) in dynamic cloud computing environments. The mechanism operates through the mediation of adaptive strategies, which allow agents to share information and optimize resource distribution collaboratively. System-level outcomes, such as resource utilization efficiency, are influenced by the technical mechanisms of adaptive learning and communication among agents. User-level outcomes, such as satisfaction with video streaming quality, are mediated by behavioral mechanisms like perceived responsiveness to workload changes. The theoretical framework is grounded in game theory and cooperative learning, suggesting that collaboration among agents can lead to improved performance. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of collaborative incentives in real-world scenarios and the stability of agent interactions under varying workloads.
hypothesis: Integrating collaborative incentives within a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning framework will significantly improve resource allocation efficiency, as measured by system utility and throughput, compared to traditional static resource allocation methods, with adaptive strategies mediating this effect.

The experimental design will include a control group utilizing existing MARL algorithms without collaborative incentives, allowing for a direct comparison of resource allocation efficiency and system performance. Key operationalized variables include resource allocation efficiency, measured by system utility and throughput, and quality of service (QoS) assessed through user satisfaction surveys. Evaluation metrics will include statistical analyses of performance metrics to validate improvements in scalability and adaptability under varying user demands. Confounding factors such as variability in user demand patterns and external environmental influences will be controlled through simulation scenarios that mimic real-world conditions. The study aims for reproducibility by documenting the MARL framework's development process and providing access to simulation logs. proposal: This research proposes the development of a novel Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing environments, specifically targeting video streaming applications. The core concepts include MARL, dynamic resource allocation, collaborative incentives, system utility, throughput, scalability, and adaptability. The study is technically feasible, requiring access to open-source MARL frameworks and GPU resources for model training, without the need for human participants or labeled datasets. The literature indicates a significant gap in adaptive strategies for dynamic workloads and the integration of collaborative incentives, which this research aims to address. The central research question is: How does the integration of collaborative incentives within a MARL framework affect resource allocation efficiency and system performance in dynamic cloud computing environments for video streaming applications compared to traditional static resource allocation methods? The theoretical mechanism posits that collaborative incentives enhance adaptive strategies, leading to improved resource allocation efficiency (system-level outcome) and user satisfaction with video streaming quality (user-level outcome). The falsifiable hypothesis states that integrating collaborative incentives will significantly improve resource allocation efficiency, as measured by system utility and throughput, compared to traditional methods. Construct operationalization includes metrics for collaborative incentives, adaptive strategies, resource allocation efficiency, and quality of service, with data sourced from simulation logs and user feedback. The methodology involves developing the MARL framework, conducting ablation studies, and comparing performance against existing MARL algorithms without collaborative incentives, ensuring robust statistical methods and confound controls. Expected contributions include theoretical advancements in cooperative learning, technical innovations in adaptive MARL algorithms, empirical validation of collaborative incentives, and practical deployment guidelines for cloud environments. Key limitations include variability in user demand patterns and potential misinterpretation of negative results, which will be mitigated through robust simulation scenarios and thorough documentation of experimental conditions.
